beats.narration_text: Six terms. A G P U is the chip that draws graphics. A pixel is one dot of the image. A uniform is a value game code hands to a shader. The renderer is the part of Godot that draws. Headless means running Godot with no window. And a mutation is a deliberate break, to prove a test notices.

a deliberate break, to test a test

beats.act: I · Two Shaders and Their Materials
beats.narration_text: Here is the job: two shaders you write by hand, and the materials that use them, added to your game. One tints an object while a game state holds. One dresses a surface with textures.

Two file chips drop in, the example's own names signal.gdshader and surface.gdshader, each with an arrow under it. Left: the REAL pad frame of the scripted lab run (captures/lab/lab_000503.png, cropped to the pad: terracotta, the mascot standing on it) tagged 'scripted input'; on 'while a game state holds' it flips to the REAL lab_000610.png (same crop, 'gate open', the pad green). Right: the example's two REAL spheres (matte and coated; circle crops of the 14 Oct capture ev_mat_baseline.png) land under surface.gdshader, tagged 'the example, 14 Oct'. The honesty chip 'instructor example · A. I.-written' sits at the foot.

beats.act: I · Two Shaders and Their Materials
beats.narration_text: A shader is a small program the G P U runs for every pixel it draws, all at once. It sees only built-ins, uniforms and textures, and remembers nothing. So game state must arrive as a uniform.

shot.visual_intent: A 12 x 6 pixel grid (outline cells). On 'for every pixel' a terracotta dot pops in every cell at once ('every pixel'). On 'built-ins', 'uniforms', 'textures' three labelled arrows slide in from the left, one per word. On 'remembers nothing' a grey sweep line crosses the grid and clears every cell ('remembers nothing'). On 'game state must arrive' a 'game code' box lands above, one rail with one tick into every column carries the mono word 'uniform', and every cell's dot comes back together.

show.event: dots pop in all 72 cells at once

shot.motion_claim: Every cell runs at once; the sweep wipes them (no memory); one line from game code reaches every cell.

qc.sparse_reason: A build-up diagram: at the sampled midpoint only the grid and the first input have landed; the other inputs and the uniform rail land with their words.

lecture.runner_up: Isometric conveyor (show-tell iso kit): built-ins, uniforms and textures riding belts into a GPU box
lecture.why: The idea is parallelism plus no memory plus one shared value: a grid where every cell acts at once, is wiped, and then all receive the same line shows all three; a conveyor shows a queue, which is the opposite of 'all at once'.

beats.act: I · Two Shaders and Their Materials
beats.narration_text: A material pairs one shader with values for its uniforms, textures included. Many materials can share one shader. Your second shader gets two that look different.

shot.visual_intent: One shader chip (surface.gdshader, the example's file) at the left. On 'with values' a 'matte' card lands with an arrow to the chip and three rows of REAL values from matte.tres (tint = a white swatch, roughness_gain 0.9, uv_scale 1.0); on 'Many materials' a 'coated' card lands with a second arrow to the SAME chip (tint swatch of (0.45, 0.95, 0.72), roughness_gain 0.25, uv_scale 2.0, from coated.tres); on 'that look different' the two real spheres land on their cards. 'instructor example · A. I.-written' at the foot.

show.event: matte card, arrow, three value rows

beats.act: I · Two Shaders and Their Materials
beats.narration_text: A texture is a grid of numbers, and the shader decides what they mean. Colour is stored as S R G B and must be decoded first. A mask, noise or roughness map must be read as stored.

shot.visual_intent: The real 3 x 1 grey fixture (texel values 64, 128, 192, from the hint experiment's file) as three outline cells with its numbers beneath, labelled 'texture'. Two arrows fan out to two reading lanes. Top lane 'colour sRGB': a 'decode' gate; a terracotta dot travels along, pauses in the gate, then leaves. Bottom lane 'data': a terracotta dot goes straight along, 'as stored'. Conceptual only: the measured result is shown later in the film.
shot.motion_claim: The same three numbers go two ways: through a decode gate for colour, straight through for data.

qc.sparse_reason: A build-up diagram: at the sampled midpoint only the colour lane has landed; the data lane lands on 'A mask'.

lecture.runner_up: ShowTellCard comparison (Remotion): a two-column 'colour read / data read' card
lecture.why: The claim is that ONE grid is read two ways; two lanes that start at the same three cells make that visible and the dots make the difference a motion (a stop at the gate versus none).

beats.act: I · Two Shaders and Their Materials
beats.narration_text: Godot's shading language is close to G L S L. You choose a shader type instead of writing main, and the type decides which functions and built-ins exist. Hints shape the Inspector; some change what the shader receives.

shot.visual_intent: code_block of the REAL signal.gdshader lines 1-3 (first=1, size 24, real line numbers). On 'close to GLSL' a label 'close to GLSL'. On 'You choose' a terracotta ring on line 1 `shader_type spatial;`; on 'instead of writing main' a prohibition mark beside the mono word main(); on 'the type decides' two chips 'functions' and 'built-ins' with arrows down to the ringed line. On 'Hints shape' a bracket under `hint_range(0.0, 1.0)` in line 3 and a DRAWN slider labelled 'Inspector slider' (tag 'illustrative', a drawing, not the editor) whose knob moves. On 'some change' the block swaps for the REAL surface.gdshader line 3 (a sampler) with a bracket under `source_color` and the label 'changes the value'. Example chip at the foot.

show.event: bracket on hint_range + drawn slider, knob moves

shot.motion_claim: A ring lands on the type line; a bracket lands on the range hint and a drawn slider's knob moves; then a bracket lands on source_color.

lecture.why: code_block keeps the real file's lines and numbers at the type floor and lets the ring and brackets travel from the type line to the hint to the colour hint, one motion per spoken clause; ClaudeCodeBeat would show the same lines but cannot carry the drawn slider beside them.

beats.narration_text: The state: what the effect communicates, why the player needs it, and which script holds it. In the example, the pad shows charge, one script owns it, and the shader only watches.

On 'the pad shows charge' a grey-backed terracotta ring lands on the 94% frame; on 'one script owns it' a ring lands on the charge line; on 'the shader only watches' the shader card (signal.gdshader) arrives with a drawn eye, an arrow carries charge into it, and an arrow carries it on to the pad. beats.narration_text: The specification: the shader's path and type, and each uniform's name, type, hint, default, and what sets it. The example has four. Only activation comes from the game.

shot.visual_intent: The specification as a table that fills in column by column on the spoken words. Header row: `shaders/signal.gdshader` (path), `shader_type spatial;` (type, real line 1). Columns name / type / hint / default / set by land on 'each uniform's name', 'type, hint', 'hint, default', 'default, and', 'what sets it'; the four rows are signal.gdshader lines 3-6 read verbatim (activation float hint_range 0.0-1.0 default 0.0; quiet_color vec4 source_color default as a colour chip; active_color vec4 source_color chip; stripe_count float hint_range 1.0-16.0 default 8.0), numbered 3-6. Defaults are drawn from the real lines (a slider with a terracotta dot at the default; two colour chips of the real defaults x 255). 'set by': garden.gd for activation only (garden.gd line 253); 'default' for the other three. '4 uniforms' lands on 'The example has four'; a grey-backed terracotta ring lands on `garden.gd` on 'Only activation'.
shot.motion_claim: Each column of the spec lands on the word that names it; the ring on garden.gd in the 'set by' column lands on 'Only activation comes from the game'.

lecture.runner_up: ShowTellCard dashboard: four uniform cards with their five fields each
lecture.why: A specification IS a table, and the film's job is to show what a good one holds; the columns landing on their words teach the five fields in order, and drawing the range and default (slider, colour chip) from the real lines carries more than repeating the numbers.

beats.narration_text: The colour line: the one line in the fragment function that changes the colour. You write the shader from it, and predict from it. Here it mixes the stripe colour toward the active colour.

shot.visual_intent: The whole real signal.gdshader (11 lines, Menlo 20, real numbers, real indentation) in an outlined frame; only line 10 shows at first and a terracotta ring lands on it as 'the one line' is said. beats.narration_text: The material plan names each texture's role and import settings, and each uniform's type, range, default and group. Predict at least three failures, with their checks. The example predicted four: a missing colour hint, an undeclared uniform, a shader edit changing both materials, and a headless pass that cannot certify colour.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. A shader runs for every pixel and remembers nothing. A material pairs one shader with values. A texture is numbers, and the shader decides what they mean. Predict first, then break your shader to prove the tests notice. Tests prove it is wired; your eyes prove how it looks. You write the shaders; the agent never edits them.
